summary_override: Proved: a(n) mod 4 is the output of a six-state automaton on the binary digits of n with outputs 0, 1, 2 (a(n) odd iff n AND 2n = 0, then a(n) = 1 mod 4).
notes: Lagrange inversion for x = t(1-t)^2 plus (1+t) sum_k C(N-k,k) t^k (1-t)^(N-2k) = 1-(-t)^(N+1) give a(n) = [t^n] S (1-t)^(-2n-1), S = sqrt((1-3t)/(1+t)), from the self-convolution definition; S = 1+2W mod 4 (W lacunary); Rowland-Yassawi Cartier operators over Z/4 close on six states with outputs 1,1,2,2,2,0. Existence: A183161 is defined in Lean as [t^n] R (1-3t)(1-t)^(-2n-1), R = 1/sqrt((1-3t)(1+t)) = 1/((1-t) sqrt(1-4u)), u = t^2/(1-t)^2, integral via the Catalan series; the substitution x -> t(1-t)^2 is onto (Lagrange inversion + triangular injectivity), so its self-convolution is A183160; uniqueness from (A-B)(A+B) = 0. Lean: A183161_spec, A183161_unique, A183161_mod4 (A183161(n) mod 4 != 3), A183161_mod4_of_conv (any such integer sequence) and A183161_gf_mod4 (Hanna's g.f.) via OpenProblemsLib.HannaMod4 and OpenProblemsLib.AutomaticMod; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. certificate/rootseq_check.py: the Lean definition matches the 24 cached terms.
